17	---
18	
19	# Peaking and tapering in an in-season college football schedule
20	
21	## 1. The question
22	
23	How should we peak and taper in season? It splits into the game week as a small taper, how long qualities last unexposed, game-week readiness, and game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, postseason).
24	
25	The sources answer a different question: every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No meta-analysed study tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.
26	
27	## 2. Bottom line
28	
29	1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
30	2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
31	3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
32	4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
33	5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]
34	
35	## 3. Where the sources agree
36	
37	**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, sports not listed in the abstract, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP relative peak force and CMJ FT:CT.
38	
39	**Strength holds on a small dose.** Issurin, citing Fleck and Kraemer, says team-sport players hold strength 14 to 16 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-109; secondhand). **External:** Ronnestad et al. 2011 (abstract; pro soccer, n = 7 per group): one session a week kept strength and 40-m sprint for 12 weeks; one every two weeks lost both; jump height did not change in either group. **External:** Spiering et al. 2021 (abstract; mostly non-athletes): one set per exercise per week held strength up to 32 weeks at kept load; too thin for athlete advice, the authors say.
40	
41	**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.
42	
43	**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). At 72 h, flight time moved -0.7% and FT:CT -7.7% ([[research-papers/gathercole-2015-alternative-countermovement-jump-analysis-to-quantify-acute-neuromuscular-fatigue|Gathercole 2015]], p. 7; n = 8). The cost is noise: several phase and RFD variables failed reliability ([[research-papers/heishman-2020-countermovement-jump-reliability-performed-with-and-without-an-arm-swing-in-ncaa-division|Heishman 2020]], pp. 5-12). ACWR did no better than an intercept-only model ([[research-papers/impellizzeri-2020-acute-to-random-workload-ratio-is-as-associated-with-injury-as-acute-to-actual-chronic-wor|Impellizzeri 2020]], pp. 4-5).
44	
45	## 4. Where they disagree
46	
47	**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday if shifted for Saturday, Inference). **External:** Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.
48	
49	**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Against: **External:** Ross and Leveritt 2001 (PDF p. 17): short-sprint detraining is "less severe than may have been reasonably anticipated". **External:** Bosquet et al. 2013 (abstract; 103 studies): cessation cut maximal power least. **External:** Ronnestad (above) kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.
50	
51	**Lifting near competition (D-5, D-7).** Platonov and Fesenko say it hurts technique; Bompa and Carrera say it keeps force ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 108). **External:** Pritchard et al. 2015 (abstract): 2 to 4 days of training cessation looks optimal for peak strength. Inference: football never stops training, so this only bounds the last lift; the shifted Issurin week puts it 4 days out.
52	
53	**Maintain or build.** **External:** Ronnestad and Spiering (above) maintain on one session; Issurin uses two. **External:** Hoffman et al. 2003 (abstract, partly garbled; freshmen, n = 14 per group, 2 sessions a week): linear training raised 1RM squat 13.8 ± 7.4 kg, nonlinear did not. Inference: building may suit low-snap freshmen.
54	
55	**Timing models.** [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported], [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested] and [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested] disagree on whether adaptation timing is predictable. Inference: mental models, not a clock.
56	
57	## 5. What transfers and what does not
58	
59	**Transfers:** the two-mini-block week as a template, cutting volume not intensity, CMJ strategy metrics. Body mass is not a taper marker: fat mass rose 4.3% at stable mass over 2 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported], PDF pp. 126-127; triathletes, n = 16, no significance test).
60	
61	**Does not transfer:** single-peak prescriptions (1 to 3 week realization, kayak dosages, 4 to 12 week delayed gains per Siff and Verkhoshansky, cited by [[periodization--bompa/principle--concentrated-loading-overreaching|Bompa]] [supported], and the 3% taper gain in **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003) assume one target event.
62	
63	**The exception, a bowl.** **External:** Marrier et al. 2017 (abstract; 10 rugby sevens players, 3-week taper): 70 to 80% of peaks fell in the first 2 weeks. **External:** Vachon et al. 2021 (abstract; 14 team-sport studies): moderate gains in power, change of direction and VO2max; no best strategy. **External:** Haugen et al. 2019 (PDF p. 11): 2 to 3 weeks for strength and power sports; smaller gains in sprinters. Fitz-Clarke 1991 finds usual tapers "may be too rigorous and short" ([[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported], printed pp. 88-89). Inference: 1 to 3 weeks, speed and heavy lifting kept, not judged by sprint times alone.
64	
65	## 6. What none of them covers
66	
67	- **Bye weeks.** **External:** Peterson (grey literature, unverified year; 108 D-I players) found a group x time interaction on a CMJ stretch-shortening factor: the gap between big and skill or mid-size players widened after the bye and persisted 24 h after the next game (PDF p. 52, Table 6). Within-group change is not tested there. Inference: dose byes by position and keep a speed or repeated-sprint exposure, given Saldanha.
68	- **Short weeks, camp to week 1, position groups, low-snap players.** Only descriptive or off-population data: [[research-papers/galiano-2026-more-matches-less-time-how-load-ratios-reveal-gaps-between-training-and-competition-in-foo|Galiano 2026]], [[research-papers/claudino-2016-autoregulating-jump-performance-to-induce-functional-overreaching|Claudino 2016]], [[research-papers/merrigan-2022-comparisons-of-countermovement-jump-force-time-characteristics-among-national-collegiate-a|Merrigan 2022]], [[research-papers/lever-2026-game-exposure-shapes-intensity-and-performance-in-division-i-college-football|Lever 2026]], and [[research-papers/aychman-2026-multimodal-indicators-of-non-functional-overreaching-in-ncaa-division-i-american-football|Aychman 2026]] (non-starters recovered worse on lower load; one program, exploratory, pp. 1, 9).
69	- **Postseason.** Bowl structure is Inference from kayak calendars; after a long layoff, rebuild contact over 3 to 4 weeks ([[research-papers/stokes-2020-returning-to-play-after-prolonged-training-restrictions-in-professional-collision-sports|Stokes 2020]], p. 7; expert opinion).
70	- **Season-long detraining.** Only the 14 to 16 week figure and Hoffman 2003; nothing on starters' speed.
71	
72	Would fill: Bompa Ch 7, Issurin Ch 4; others in the evidence map, Gaps.
73	
74	## 7. Eric's baseline
75	
76	- **Eric's baseline:** daily CMJ mRSI is the readiness marker, "objective, consistent, and actionable" (SportSmith piece); athletes gamed wellness surveys. Inference: matches section 3 and [[research-papers/mccall-2023-a-qualitative-study-of-11-world-class-team-sport-athletes-experiences-answering-subjective|McCall 2023]].
77	- **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic is lost fastest, speed slowest; that order sets re-exposure. Conflicts with Issurin.
78	- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** speed every 5 days, aerobic and strength every 30 (class-1 p. 27). These are Issurin's Table 1.6 reproduced in the slides (week1-lecture p. 66), not independent support, and class-1 also says aerobic is gained and lost quickly (pp. 25, 28). The real disagreement is class-4 p. 47 against Issurin.
79	- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** "maintain intensity, reduce volume", a strength retention dose, a waved week (class-1 pp. 17-25; class-8 p. 21). Agrees with section 3.
80	- **Eric's baseline (class-4 slides, pp. 34, 39):** conditioning targets alactic and aerobic capacity. Inference: fits the 1:7 ratio in 2004 D-I games ([[research-papers/iosia-2008-analysis-of-exercise-to-rest-ratios-during-division-ia-televised-football-competition|Iosia 2008]]).
81	
82	## 8. Questions for Eric
83	
84	1. Does "peak" mean every Saturday, target games, or only the postseason?
85	2. Issurin's week, shifted for Saturday (Inference), lifts Monday and Tuesday, 48 and 72 h post-game, while fast force is still down. Where do our heaviest lifts and practice sit, and should heavy and high-velocity work wait until Wednesday?
86	3. Class-4 (p. 47) says aerobic is lost fastest; the course's 5 and 30 day figures are Issurin's table, and class-1 says aerobic goes quickly too. Is class-4 your view, and are the course in-season rules yours?
87	4. How are bye weeks used now (restoration, loading, or a speed and strength top-up), and by position?
88	5. Which mRSI drop, on which day, changes the plan, and do linemen and low-snap players get their own thresholds?
89	6. Does the postseason get a distinct 1 to 3 week taper?
90	
91	## 9. Sources used
92	
93	Library entries: [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky fatigue]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested]; [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported]; [[periodization--bompa/principle--concentrated-loading-overreaching|Bompa loading]] [supported]; [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested].
94	
95	Paper briefs: linked in text.
96	
97	External (labelled in text): Bosquet 2007, 2013; Mujika and Padilla 2000, 2003; Vachon 2021; Marrier 2017; Pritchard 2015, 2019; Haugen 2019; Pyne 2009; Ronnestad 2011; Spiering 2021; Cuthbert 2024; Wellman 2019; Hoffman 2003; Peterson; Ross and Leveritt 2001; Saldanha 2026. Baseline: `docs/method-baseline.md`.

# Peaking and tapering in an in-season college football schedule

## 1. The question

How should we peak and taper in season? It splits into the game week as a small taper, how long qualities last unexposed, game-week readiness, and game-free windows (byes, camp to week 1, postseason).

The sources answer a different question: every peaking model in the library comes from individual-event sports (kayak, swimming, track and field). **External:** Pyne, Mujika and Reilly 2009 (abstract): taper research does not yet guide a league season. **External:** Cuthbert et al. 2024 (PDF p. 5): a season-long peak is unrealistic. No meta-analysed study tested whether adaptations peaked when predicted ([[research-papers/afonso-2019-a-systematic-review-of-meta-analyses-comparing-periodized-and-non-periodized-exercise-prog|Afonso 2019]], pp. 1, 4). So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]

## 3. Where the sources agree

**Cut volume, keep intensity.** Issurin's pre-competitive week cuts volume, keeps frequency and raises the max-speed share ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 105). **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003 (abstract): volume down 60 to 90%, frequency down at most 20%. **External:** Bosquet et al. 2007 (abstract; 27 studies, sports not listed in the abstract, mostly endurance per the evidence file): 2 weeks, volume down 41 to 60%. **External:** Pritchard et al. 2019 (abstract; 11 strength-trained men, 1-week taper, about 70% volume cut): tapers did not differ significantly; only the higher-intensity one showed small effect-size gains in IMTP relative peak force and CMJ FT:CT.

**Strength holds on a small dose.** Issurin, citing Fleck and Kraemer, says team-sport players hold strength 14 to 16 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-109; secondhand). **External:** Ronnestad et al. 2011 (abstract; pro soccer, n = 7 per group): one session a week kept strength and 40-m sprint for 12 weeks; one every two weeks lost both; jump height did not change in either group. **External:** Spiering et al. 2021 (abstract; mostly non-athletes): one set per exercise per week held strength up to 32 weeks at kept load; too thin for athlete advice, the authors say.

**Heavy early, light late.** For a Sunday game, Issurin (citing Baker 2001, rugby league) lifts Tuesday and Wednesday mornings, holds the key practice ("substantial or big" load) Thursday afternoon, and restricts only the pre-game session ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported], PDF pp. 108-111). Inference: for Saturday, lifts move to Monday and Tuesday, key practice to Wednesday. **External:** Wellman et al. 2019 (31 D-I players, one program, PDF p. 6): late-season Tuesday and Wednesday loads fell by a planned duration cut; Thursday did not change.

**Strategy metrics beat output.** Jump height fell only slightly by 24 h while RSImod and FT:CT stayed down ([[research-papers/lewis-undated-athlete-monitoring-in-american-collegiate-football|Lewis]], pp. 96-97; n = 5). At 72 h, flight time moved -0.7% and FT:CT -7.7% ([[research-papers/gathercole-2015-alternative-countermovement-jump-analysis-to-quantify-acute-neuromuscular-fatigue|Gathercole 2015]], p. 7; n = 8). The cost is noise: several phase and RFD variables failed reliability ([[research-papers/heishman-2020-countermovement-jump-reliability-performed-with-and-without-an-arm-swing-in-ncaa-division|Heishman 2020]], pp. 5-12). ACWR did no better than an intercept-only model ([[research-papers/impellizzeri-2020-acute-to-random-workload-ratio-is-as-associated-with-injury-as-acute-to-actual-chronic-wor|Impellizzeri 2020]], pp. 4-5).

## 4. Where they disagree

**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday if shifted for Saturday, Inference). **External:** Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.

**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Against: **External:** Ross and Leveritt 2001 (PDF p. 17): short-sprint detraining is "less severe than may have been reasonably anticipated". **External:** Bosquet et al. 2013 (abstract; 103 studies): cessation cut maximal power least. **External:** Ronnestad (above) kept sprint without max-velocity work. The residual entry notes these may measure cessation versus a retention dose; Issurin calls residual-only design "extremely rigid and inflexible" ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported], PDF p. 127). Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

**Lifting near competition (D-5, D-7).** Platonov and Fesenko say it hurts technique; Bompa and Carrera say it keeps force ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported], PDF p. 108). **External:** Pritchard et al. 2015 (abstract): 2 to 4 days of training cessation looks optimal for peak strength. Inference: football never stops training, so this only bounds the last lift; the shifted Issurin week puts it 4 days out.

**Maintain or build.** **External:** Ronnestad and Spiering (above) maintain on one session; Issurin uses two. **External:** Hoffman et al. 2003 (abstract, partly garbled; freshmen, n = 14 per group, 2 sessions a week): linear training raised 1RM squat 13.8 ± 7.4 kg, nonlinear did not. Inference: building may suit low-snap freshmen.

**Timing models.** [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported], [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested] and [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested] disagree on whether adaptation timing is predictable. Inference: mental models, not a clock.

## 5. What transfers and what does not

**Transfers:** the two-mini-block week as a template, cutting volume not intensity, CMJ strategy metrics. Body mass is not a taper marker: fat mass rose 4.3% at stable mass over 2 weeks ([[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported], PDF pp. 126-127; triathletes, n = 16, no significance test).

**Does not transfer:** single-peak prescriptions (1 to 3 week realization, kayak dosages, 4 to 12 week delayed gains per Siff and Verkhoshansky, cited by [[periodization--bompa/principle--concentrated-loading-overreaching|Bompa]] [supported], and the 3% taper gain in **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2003) assume one target event.

**The exception, a bowl.** **External:** Marrier et al. 2017 (abstract; 10 rugby sevens players, 3-week taper): 70 to 80% of peaks fell in the first 2 weeks. **External:** Vachon et al. 2021 (abstract; 14 team-sport studies): moderate gains in power, change of direction and VO2max; no best strategy. **External:** Haugen et al. 2019 (PDF p. 11): 2 to 3 weeks for strength and power sports; smaller gains in sprinters. Fitz-Clarke 1991 finds usual tapers "may be too rigorous and short" ([[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported], printed pp. 88-89). Inference: 1 to 3 weeks, speed and heavy lifting kept, not judged by sprint times alone.

## 6. What none of them covers

- **Bye weeks.** **External:** Peterson (grey literature, unverified year; 108 D-I players) found a group x time interaction on a CMJ stretch-shortening factor: the gap between big and skill or mid-size players widened after the bye and persisted 24 h after the next game (PDF p. 52, Table 6). Within-group change is not tested there. Inference: dose byes by position and keep a speed or repeated-sprint exposure, given Saldanha.
- **Short weeks, camp to week 1, position groups, low-snap players.** Only descriptive or off-population data: [[research-papers/galiano-2026-more-matches-less-time-how-load-ratios-reveal-gaps-between-training-and-competition-in-foo|Galiano 2026]], [[research-papers/claudino-2016-autoregulating-jump-performance-to-induce-functional-overreaching|Claudino 2016]], [[research-papers/merrigan-2022-comparisons-of-countermovement-jump-force-time-characteristics-among-national-collegiate-a|Merrigan 2022]], [[research-papers/lever-2026-game-exposure-shapes-intensity-and-performance-in-division-i-college-football|Lever 2026]], and [[research-papers/aychman-2026-multimodal-indicators-of-non-functional-overreaching-in-ncaa-division-i-american-football|Aychman 2026]] (non-starters recovered worse on lower load; one program, exploratory, pp. 1, 9).
- **Postseason.** Bowl structure is Inference from kayak calendars; after a long layoff, rebuild contact over 3 to 4 weeks ([[research-papers/stokes-2020-returning-to-play-after-prolonged-training-restrictions-in-professional-collision-sports|Stokes 2020]], p. 7; expert opinion).
- **Season-long detraining.** Only the 14 to 16 week figure and Hoffman 2003; nothing on starters' speed.

Would fill: Bompa Ch 7, Issurin Ch 4; others in the evidence map, Gaps.

## 7. Eric's baseline

- **Eric's baseline:** daily CMJ mRSI is the readiness marker, "objective, consistent, and actionable" (SportSmith piece); athletes gamed wellness surveys. Inference: matches section 3 and [[research-papers/mccall-2023-a-qualitative-study-of-11-world-class-team-sport-athletes-experiences-answering-subjective|McCall 2023]].
- **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic is lost fastest, speed slowest; that order sets re-exposure. Conflicts with Issurin.
- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** speed every 5 days, aerobic and strength every 30 (class-1 p. 27). These are Issurin's Table 1.6 reproduced in the slides (week1-lecture p. 66), not independent support, and class-1 also says aerobic is gained and lost quickly (pp. 25, 28). The real disagreement is class-4 p. 47 against Issurin.
- **Course baseline (HHPR 5355, speaker unconfirmed):** "maintain intensity, reduce volume", a strength retention dose, a waved week (class-1 pp. 17-25; class-8 p. 21). Agrees with section 3.
- **Eric's baseline (class-4 slides, pp. 34, 39):** conditioning targets alactic and aerobic capacity. Inference: fits the 1:7 ratio in 2004 D-I games ([[research-papers/iosia-2008-analysis-of-exercise-to-rest-ratios-during-division-ia-televised-football-competition|Iosia 2008]]).

## 8. Questions for Eric

1. Does "peak" mean every Saturday, target games, or only the postseason?
2. Issurin's week, shifted for Saturday (Inference), lifts Monday and Tuesday, 48 and 72 h post-game, while fast force is still down. Where do our heaviest lifts and practice sit, and should heavy and high-velocity work wait until Wednesday?
3. Class-4 (p. 47) says aerobic is lost fastest; the course's 5 and 30 day figures are Issurin's table, and class-1 says aerobic goes quickly too. Is class-4 your view, and are the course in-season rules yours?
4. How are bye weeks used now (restoration, loading, or a speed and strength top-up), and by position?
5. Which mRSI drop, on which day, changes the plan, and do linemen and low-snap players get their own thresholds?
6. Does the postseason get a distinct 1 to 3 week taper?

## 9. Sources used

Library entries: [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--realization-mesocycle-taper-prescription|Issurin realization]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--pre-competitive-microcycle-tuning|Issurin pre-competitive]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--in-season-team-sport-mini-block-microcycle|Issurin in-season]] [supported]; [[block-periodization--issurin/framework--prolonging-residual-effects-with-mini-blocks|Issurin mini-blocks]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky fatigue]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--fitness-fatigue-modeling-and-taper-timing|Verkhoshansky taper]] [supported]; [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation|Verkhoshansky]] [contested]; [[periodization--bompa/principle--supercompensation-cycle|Bompa]] [supported]; [[periodization--bompa/principle--concentrated-loading-overreaching|Bompa loading]] [supported]; [[elite-sports-performance--evans/claim--fitness-fatigue-model-is-unvalidated-concept|Evans]] [untested].

Paper briefs: linked in text.

External (labelled in text): Bosquet 2007, 2013; Mujika and Padilla 2000, 2003; Vachon 2021; Marrier 2017; Pritchard 2015, 2019; Haugen 2019; Pyne 2009; Ronnestad 2011; Spiering 2021; Cuthbert 2024; Wellman 2019; Hoffman 2003; Peterson; Ross and Leveritt 2001; Saldanha 2026. Baseline: `docs/method-baseline.md`.

- Exercise selection is organized on a spectrum from general preparation through specific preparation, specific development, to competitive exercises (Bondarchuk), replacing the loose and often-misapplied idea of "sport specific." **Inferred (transcript + slides)** [01192022-hp5355-class1-transcript.md pp.13-16; week1-lecture.md pp.32-36]

- The Principle of Dynamic Correspondence (Verkhoshansky) — matching amplitude/direction of movement, region of force production, dynamics of effort, rate/timing of force production, and regime of muscular work to the sport skill — governs whether an exercise actually transfers, rather than surface resemblance to the sport. **Inferred (transcript + slides)** [01192022-hp5355-class1-transcript.md p.14; week1-lecture.md p.34]

- Training time is deliberately weighted toward high motor-unit-recruitment core/ballistic movements (squats, cleans, jumps, throws, sprints); single-joint assistance work is kept to a small share of total volume. **Inferred (transcript + slides)** [01192022-hp5355-class1-transcript.md p.13; week1-lecture.md p.31]

lines: - Conditioning is defined two ways: (1) how well an athlete can meet the energy requirements of their specific sport/activity, and (2) how well they sustain strength, speed, and power output across a full competition. **Explicit** [week3-lecture.md p.22]

- All three energy systems (alactic ~10-12s highest power, glycolytic/anaerobic-lactic ~60-90s medium capacity, aerobic hours-long lowest power/highest capacity) are always active simultaneously; programming targets the adaptation, not the drill label. **Explicit** [week3-lecture.md p.19; class-4-2026.md p.15]

- A sport cannot maximize all three energy systems at once — priority has to be picked based on what the competition actually demands (e.g., for football: prepared for fall camp first, then the first game). **Explicit** [class-4-2026.md p.31]

-- For football specifically, the stated priority stack is: Goal 1, alactic and aerobic capacity/power for fall-camp demands; Goal 2, the same two systems for game demands; glycolytic conditioning is treated as a "worst case scenario" to be absorbed incidentally through camp and practice rather than programmed as a primary target. **Explicit** [class-4-2026.md pp.34, 39]

- Anaerobic (lactate) threshold heart-rate zones are assigned by athlete body size rather than a single number: roughly 165 bpm for big/tall athletes, 170 for medium, 175 for small, with Zone 1-4 bands set as percentages of that individual threshold. **Explicit** [class-4-2026.md pp.28-29]

- The traits easiest to build (aerobic) are lost fastest under detraining; the traits hardest to build (alactic/speed) are lost slowest — this ordering is used to sequence what needs the most frequent re-exposure. **Explicit** [class-4-2026.md p.47]

- Training intensities between roughly 75-90% of maximal effort are labeled (via Francis) "no man's land" — too fast to build alactic power cleanly, too slow to build real aerobic capacity — and are treated as a zone to generally avoid as a primary training target. **Explicit** [class-4-2026.md p.48]

+Status after the interview (2026-09-28): resolved 1 (partly), 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9; still open 7 (partly), 8, 10. New tensions from the interview are 11 to 16. Each entry below carries its status on its last line.

1. **The task's own premise doesn't fully hold.** Both class transcripts (Class 1 and Class 3) are diarized entirely under a single Fireflies speaker label, "Chris Ruf," for every line — including Class 3, which the Spring 2026 teaching schedule assigns solo to Rash (`spring-2026-teaching.md`: "Feb. 5 | Conditioning - Alactic-Aerobic | Rash"). Fireflies likely defaulted to the meeting organizer's name instead of doing real per-speaker diarization. This means roughly 30,000 words of the richest, most first-person material in this corpus cannot be confidently attributed to Rash specifically versus Ruf or Wenger. Every transcript-sourced bullet above is marked Inferred for this reason, even where the underlying statement is a confident, first-person claim.

2. **Department reporting model is not internally consistent.** The Playbook (p.6) frames Applied Performance as a peer discipline inside Health & Wellness that "enables" Athletics Performance, Athletic Medicine, Nutrition, and Mental Health to answer their own questions. But Week 1 course material lists "Applied Performance" as one of many training sub-categories nested under Athletic Performance itself (p.11), and the same transcript narration describes Rash's role as "helping program and plan the training" — a support-staff framing, not a peer-department framing. Which model actually governs day-to-day authority is not reconciled anywhere in these documents.

So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested; no football data]. Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. Lift heaviest early; for a Saturday game the last high-volume practice falls by Wednesday, and volume, not intensity, drops from Thursday. [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program agree on early-heavy, late-light but differ on the heaviest practice day; descriptive only] Inference: about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak; untested.
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] Inference: position and starter splits rest on off-season profiles and one exploratory study.
4. Keep aerobic and repeat-effort conditioning every week; it may be lost fastest. [contested: Eric's baseline and Mujika and Padilla 2000 against Issurin]
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football]
input.new_string:
So: hold readiness weekly, and peak on purpose only in game-free windows. **Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q14):** "in football you want to peak every Saturday, but definitely throughout the month of November as you get closer to the postseason." Inference: in the sources' terms, that is readiness held high every week, with November and the postseason as the priority window and a deliberate peak only where a game-free gap allows one.

## 2. Bottom line

1. Every game week keeps one heavy lower-body session, load high, sets cut [supported direction; the tested minimum, not Issurin's two-session template; no football trial], and one planned max-velocity exposure [contested in the literature; Eric treats it as required, since he holds that speed fades first (interview Q16)]. Eric's week already has one heavy lift (Monday) plus a lighter Wednesday lift (interview Q15). Inference: prioritize positions that rarely reach top speed in games.
2. **Eric's week (interview 2026-09-28, Q15):** Sunday off; Monday heavy lift; Tuesday and Wednesday heavy practice, with a lighter lift Wednesday; lifting and hard practice end 72 h before a Saturday kickoff. This is the sources' early-heavy, late-light shape [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program; descriptive only]. Rev 2 inferred about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak. Inference: Eric's 72 h (3 days) sits inside Pritchard's range and is longer than the rev 2 guess; untested in football. Tension: the Monday heavy lift falls about 48 h post-game, inside the window where Norris 2019 and Cosio 2026 report fast-force and hamstring deficits (section 4).
3. Read readiness from CMJ strategy metrics (mRSI or RSImod, FT:CT), no arm swing, against each player's norm, not jump height alone or ACWR. They are noisier, so set thresholds from each player's typical error. [supported direction; small football samples] **Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q2, Q2a):** the read is on Wednesdays, with individualized thresholds: "Percent change from baseline or a rolling average. We've used standard deviations and SWC to diagnose signal versus noise." This matches the sources. Inference: Wednesday is about 96 h post-game, after the Monday lift and Tuesday practice, so it reads the accumulated week, not game recovery alone.
4. **Eric's position (interview 2026-09-28, Q16):** speed fades first, per Issurin, and that drives in-season sprint recommendations; so max-velocity exposure recurs within Issurin's 5 ± 3 day window. The literature stays split [contested: Issurin and, loosely, Saldanha 2026 for speed first; Mujika and Padilla 2000, Ross and Leveritt 2001 and Bosquet 2013 against]. Inference: Mujika and Padilla 2000 (VO2max falls within 4 weeks) still argues for some aerobic and repeat-effort work each week; heavy practice may already supply it, which our GPS could check.
5. Save a real taper (about 1 to 3 weeks, volume down 40 to 60%, intensity kept) for one peak after a game-free gap, such as a bowl. [supported in other sports; untested in football] Eric names the postseason as the priority window (Q14) but did not say whether it gets a distinct taper.

lines: ## 4. Where they disagree

-**Heaviest practice day, and the post-game window.** Issurin's key practice is late (Wednesday if shifted for Saturday, Inference). **External:** Wellman's program planned Tuesday as its highest practice (PDF p. 6); Lewis (PDF p. 86) found Tuesday and Wednesday closest to game demands for linemen. Both sit in the post-game window: after AFL matches, IMTP RFD (0 to 50 ms) was still down 17.8% at 72 h and 16.9% at 96 h, CV 16.4% ([[research-papers/norris-2019-recovery-of-forcetime-characteristics-after-australian-rules-football-matches-examining-th|Norris 2019]], p. 2); after soccer, hamstring RTD and sprint were impaired at 72 h ([[research-papers/cosio-2026-transcriptomic-profiling-of-the-biceps-femoris-long-head-72-h-following-a-football-match-a|Cosio 2026]], p. 8; n = 9, no control). After Saturday, Monday is about 48 h, Tuesday 72, Wednesday 96. Unresolved: load incompletely recovered players by design (Issurin), or hold heavy and high-velocity work until Wednesday? Settle with our CMJ and sprint data by hours post-game.

**Which quality goes first (D-6).** Issurin: speed (5 ± 3 days) before aerobic and strength (30 ± 5), no sample ([[block-periodization--issurin/claim--residual-training-effect-durations-by-motor-ability|Issurin residuals]] [contested], PDF p. 35). **Eric's baseline (class-4-2026 slides, p. 47):** aerobic first, speed last. **External:** Mujika and Padilla 2000 (abstract): within 4 weeks, trained athletes lose VO2max fast, strength little. Inference: sides with class 4. **External:** Saldanha et al. 2026 (abstract; 17 to 21 semi-pro soccer players, uncontrolled): after 5 days off, repeated-sprint time and RAST peak velocity worsened; jump and hip adductor and abductor strength held. Inference: leans toward Issurin, though RAST is not a max-velocity test. Settle with our data around byes and winter break.

## 8. Questions for Eric

1. Does "peak" mean every Saturday, target games, or only the postseason?
2. Issurin's week, shifted for Saturday (Inference), lifts Monday and Tuesday, 48 and 72 h post-game, while fast force is still down. Where do our heaviest lifts and practice sit, and should heavy and high-velocity work wait until Wednesday?
3. Class-4 (p. 47) says aerobic is lost fastest; the course's 5 and 30 day figures are Issurin's table, and class-1 says aerobic goes quickly too. Is class-4 your view, and are the course in-season rules yours?
4. How are bye weeks used now (restoration, loading, or a speed and strength top-up), and by position?
5. Which mRSI drop, on which day, changes the plan, and do linemen and low-snap players get their own thresholds?
6. Does the postseason get a distinct 1 to 3 week taper?
input.new_string:
## 8. Eric's answers (interview 2026-09-28)

The rev 2 questions, answered in `docs/interview/2026-09-28-method-interview.md`.

1. **What "peak" means (Q14).** Every Saturday, and above all through November into the postseason: "That's when players need to be at or near their peak as they head into the postseason and playoffs."
2. **Where the heavy work sits (Q15).** Sunday off; Monday heavy lift; Tuesday and Wednesday heavy practice, lighter lift Wednesday; lifting and hard practice end 72 h before kickoff. He did not say whether heavy work should wait until Wednesday; the week as run does not. The section 4 tension stays open.
3. **Which quality fades first (Q16).** "I believe Issurin." Class-4 p. 47 is superseded for Eric. The course in-season rules ("maintain intensity, reduce volume") were not claimed, and the in-season sets and reps are not available (Q18).
4. **Bye weeks (Q17).** Three practices, extra rest and recovery, slightly higher volume than a game week, a speed and strength top-up, harder for low-snap players. Dosed by snaps, not by position.
5. **mRSI rule (Q2, Q2a).** Wednesdays, individualized thresholds: "Percent change from baseline or a rolling average. We've used standard deviations and SWC to diagnose signal versus noise." No numeric trigger was given, and no separate linemen or low-snap thresholds beyond individualization.
6. **A distinct postseason taper.** Not answered directly. Q14 names the postseason as the priority window only.

Still open for Eric: whether the postseason gets its own 1 to 3 week taper; the in-season strength dose (Q18); whether the Monday heavy lift at about 48 h post-game is worth checking against a Monday CMJ read.

The rev 2 questions, answered in `docs/interview/2026-09-28-method-interview.md`.

1. **What "peak" means (Q14).** Every Saturday, and above all through November into the postseason: "That's when players need to be at or near their peak as they head into the postseason and playoffs."
2. **Where the heavy work sits (Q15).** Sunday off; Monday heavy lift; Tuesday and Wednesday heavy practice, lighter lift Wednesday; lifting and hard practice end 72 h before kickoff. He did not say whether heavy work should wait until Wednesday; the week as run does not. The section 4 tension stays open.
3. **Which quality fades first (Q16).** "I believe Issurin." Class-4 p. 47 is superseded for Eric. The course in-season rules ("maintain intensity, reduce volume") were not claimed, and the in-season sets and reps are not available (Q18).
4. **Bye weeks (Q17).** Three practices, extra rest and recovery, slightly higher volume than a game week, a speed and strength top-up, harder for low-snap players. Dosed by snaps, not by position.
5. **mRSI rule (Q2, Q2a).** Wednesdays, individualized thresholds: "Percent change from baseline or a rolling average. We've used standard deviations and SWC to diagnose signal versus noise." No numeric trigger was given, and no separate linemen or low-snap thresholds beyond individualization.
6. **A distinct postseason taper.** Not answered directly. Q14 names the postseason as the priority window only.

Still open for Eric: whether the postseason gets its own 1 to 3 week taper; the in-season strength dose (Q18); whether the Monday heavy lift at about 48 h post-game is worth checking against a Monday CMJ read.

2. **Eric's week (interview 2026-09-28, Q15):** Sunday off; Monday heavy lift; Tuesday and Wednesday heavy practice, with a lighter lift Wednesday; lifting and hard practice end 72 h before a Saturday kickoff. This is the sources' early-heavy, late-light shape [Issurin (rugby league) and one D-I program; descriptive only]. Rev 2 inferred about 48 h from the last heavy session to kickoff, from [[supertraining--verkhoshansky/framework--central-vs-peripheral-fatigue-mechanisms|Verkhoshansky's]] [supported] 48 h recovery after high-CNS work (printed p. 15) and Pritchard 2015's 2 to 4 days of cessation before a strength peak. [supported direction; small football samples] **Eric (interview 2026-09-28, Q2, Q2a):** the read is on Wednesdays, with individualized thresholds: "Percent change from baseline or a rolling average. 4. **Eric's position (interview 2026-09-28, Q16):** speed fades first, per Issurin, and that drives in-season sprint recommendations. Inference: by that rule, max-velocity exposure recurs within Issurin's 5 ± 3 day window (PDF p. 35). The literature stays split [contested: Issurin and, loosely, Saldanha 2026 for speed first; Mujika and Padilla 2000, Ross and Leveritt 2001 and Bosquet 2013 against]. Inference: Mujika and Padilla 2000 (VO2max falls within 4 weeks) still argues for some aerobic and repeat-effort work each week; heavy practice may already supply it, which our GPS could check.

content.text:
I've applied all of Eric's interview answers and committed them on step1-triage in two commits, 5545f06 and 4ac2693. Nothing was pushed, and the vault was not touched.

**`docs/method-baseline.md`**
- **Inferred to Explicit:** 3 bullets (Vermeil hierarchy, undulating periodization, Dynamic Correspondence). The football energy-system stack was already Explicit; I added that he claimed it again in Q1.
- **Legacy:** 11 bullets. That covers 7 from Assessment Manual V12, the V4 table (Q9 says it was never used), the 1RM assumptions, TMG (Chris Ruf with Track only) and the five expectations.
- **Superseded:** 2 bullets from his own slides. The body-size heart-rate table (pp.28-29) is replaced by his age-based answer (Q20). The "aerobic lost first" slide (p.47) is replaced by his Issurin answer (Q16).
- **New:** 26 bullets covering every item on your list, plus Q5 ("Both") and Q25 (constraints-led coaching not used).
- **Tensions:** each of the original 10 now has a status line. Resolved: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, and 1 partly. Still open: 7, 8, 10. I added new tensions 11 to 16.
- **Thin flags:** injury risk, recovery and nutrition now say plainly that nothing formal exists. RTP has a stated role, but its written protocol (the UE and LE templates) is not staged yet.
- The provenance key has the new tags, and the named-influences table now credits Eric for Vermeil, Verkhoshansky and Parker, and has a new Issurin row.

**Peaking synthesis rev 3 (dated 2026-09-28)**
- Section 8 is replaced with his answers.
- The bottom line now uses his real week, with 72 h replacing the 48 h rev 2 guessed.
- The Monday heavy lift at about 48 h post-game is recorded as a labelled tension against Norris 2019 and Cosio 2026, with no verdict.
- Bottom line 4 now gives his Issurin position and keeps the counter-evidence. Sections 4, 6 and 7 are updated, and no new evidence was added.

**`docs/interview-prep.md`:** one-line completion note at the top pointing to the answers file.

**Answers I could not map cleanly**
- **Q7:** he said thresholds do not exist "formally". The question also asked about informal ones, and that half went unanswered.
- **Peaking Q3, second half:** the course's in-season rule ("maintain intensity, reduce volume") was never claimed.
- **Peaking Q6:** whether the postseason gets its own taper was not answered.
- **Q18:** he doesn't have the in-season sets and reps.
- **Q21:** he answered with DSI (CMJ against mid-thigh pull), not the SJ-CMJ gap the question asked about. DSI has no evidence check in the library yet.

**Contradictions**
- **His answers against his own teaching:** Q16 and Q20 each contradict slides from a session he taught himself (p.47 and pp.28-29).
- **Q2 against SportSmith:** he names a Wednesday mRSI read, but his SportSmith piece describes daily mRSI readiness.
- **Q22 against Q2:** "We don't assess readiness" (in RTP) sits against mRSI as his readiness marker.
- **Q4 against the Playbook:** "It doesn't really end" goes further than the Playbook's "support" framing.
- **Q3 against Q12:** by his own rule, a test that answers no question has no place. Yet the staff still look at ACWR ("we dabble") while he doesn't trust it, and movement screens are collected without changing decisions.
- **Q10 against %1RM loading:** no sport tests a true 1RM, yet the loading charts in his course material are written as percentages of it. So in practice those loads rest on projected maxes.

The synthesis's revision log in `_work/review_peaking_synthesis_opus.md` still stops at rev 2, and `docs/STATUS.md` is not updated.
